source.section: PA-40 lines 1a to 12 (form pages 1-2); PDF page 1 and form line 12 rate 3.07 percent; PDF page 9 no standard deduction or exemptions; PDF page 20 Lines 9 and 10; PDF page 21 Lines 11 and 12; PDF page 12 'Individual Retirement Accounts', Withdrawals, item 1; PDF page 14 IMPORTANT (retired before 59 1/2: cost recovery until 59 1/2)

worked: IRA withdrawal at 60: exempt. Federal AGI = wages person 0 40,000.00 + IRA distribution person 0 30,000.00 = 70,000.00. Federal taxable income = 70,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 54,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Pennsylvania, as the projection works it: start federal AGI 70,000.00; less 30,000.00 IRA distribution person 0 (born 1965-06-15, 59 1/2 on 2024-12-15) (pa_ira_from_59_5); income after reliefs = 40,000.00. No standard deduction or exemption (PDF page 9), no Line 10 deduction: state taxable income 40,000.00. Tax = 40,000.00 x 0.0307 = 1,228.00. No credit in the projection; state income tax 1,228.00. Form: Line 1a/1c 40,000.00; Line 2 0.00; Line 3 0.00; Line 5 0.00; Line 9 40,000.00; Line 10 0.00; Line 11 40,000.00; Line 12 1,228.00. Schedule SP: Eligibility Income 40,000.00 is over 8,750.00, so no Tax Forgiveness on the form either.
accepted_approximations: Pennsylvania has no federal starting point: it adds the positive amounts of eight classes (compensation, interest, dividends, business, gains, rents, estates and trusts, gambling). The mapping runs from federal AGI to those classes: start from federal AGI, then take out what the reliefs below exempt. Wages, interest, dividends, gains, business income and rents are taken as federal AGI holds them, in one sum. The differences that remain are listed one by one in the next four entries.
